thread.title: Apple iPhone Inventories Go 'From Bad To Worse', Carrier Survey Shows

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple iPhone Inventories Go 'From Bad To Worse', Carrier Survey Shows
text:
A survey of wireless carriers by an investment bank showed increasingly disappointing demand for the latest Apple iPhone models, resulting in spiking retail inventories in North America and Western Europe.
X In a report late Tuesday, KeyBanc Capital Markets analyst John Vinh said Apple 's ( AAPL ) latest inventories for iPhones "went from bad to worse" from November to December. His firm's latest survey showed that sales of the flagship Apple iPhone XS and XS Max handsets "slowed dramatically" in December, causing inventories to rise. Sales of the midrange Apple iPhone XR continue to be weak, as they have since launch, he noted.
"Inventories for both XS models in addition to the XR have increased significantly month to month, to over four days, which indicates this could be one of the most disappointing phone cycles since the (iPhone) 6S," Vinh said. Carriers offered limited promotions for the handsets over the holiday shopping season, he said.
The survey results are negative for Apple iPhone component suppliers, including Broadcom ( AVGO ), Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ), Qorvo ( QRVO ), Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ) and Synaptics ( SYNA ). Vinh rates Broadcom stock as overweight and the others as sector weight.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Apple To Report Fiscal First-Quarter Results Jan. 29 On Jan. 2 , Apple warned of weaker-than-expected sales for the December quarter. The Cupertino, Calif.-based company cited weak iPhone demand, especially in China, in the negative preannouncement.
Apple guided to sales of about $84 billion for its fiscal first quarter ended Dec. 29. It previously predicted sales of $89 billion to $93 billion, or $91 billion at the midpoint.
Apple is scheduled to report its holiday-quarter results after the market close on Jan. 29 .
Apple stock rose 1.2% to 154.92 on the stock market today . It hit a record high of 233.47 on Oct. 3.
